claims.statement: Current EU consumer guidance says online buyers generally have 14 days to cancel and return an order without giving a reason and that traders must refund standard delivery costs in covered cases.
Eurostat reports that 77% of EU people bought or ordered online in 2024, up from 59% in 2014, confirming a broad transaction base but not merchant return rates.
A February 2026 European Commission notice says nearly 20 million returned items are discarded annually in Germany and explicitly encourages better return handling and resale alternatives.

contrary_evidence: Consumers often bear return shipping when properly informed, so not every return creates the same merchant logistics cost.
OMS, WMS and marketplace platforms already expose return reports and basic abuse rules.
The Commission's discarded-return figure is for Germany and does not establish the Polish merchant loss distribution.

economics.acquisition_route: Run a 6-12 month historical SKU/returns analysis for one vertical, recruit two 3PL or platform agencies, then use verified avoided-return and faster-restock case metrics for channel sales.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Two hundred merchants averaging 4000 PLN monthly would create 9.6m PLN annual recurring revenue before savings fees. At a mature 38% owner-cash margin, around 3.65m PLN annually could generate over 10m PLN in cumulative distributions within four mature years without exit proceeds.
economics.founder_time: Launch with batch exports and one merchandise category at 3.5-5 hours/day, leaving customer blocking and refund decisions to merchant staff; remain employed through objective repeatability and runway gates.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Connectors, modelling and queues are software; target 70-85% gross margin after data onboarding and quarterly outcome review, with no ownership of returned inventory.
economics.payback: Target under 3 months for merchants whose annual return loss materially exceeds the subscription; attribution must separate seasonality, promotions and mix shift.
economics.pricing: Assumption to test: 2500-12000 PLN monthly by order volume plus 5-10% of loss reduction measured against a pre-agreed SKU or cohort baseline.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Returns recur with every season and product launch, and accumulated intervention history strengthens recommendations; merchant churn or platform data restrictions weaken retention.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A category-specific return-propensity and disposition-yield dataset links interventions to downstream loss, while merchant-specific customer and product data remain isolated.
fingerprint.customer: CEE online merchants processing roughly 5000-200000 physical-goods orders per month, with enough returns to employ dedicated operations staff but insufficient internal data science.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: E-commerce agencies, 3PLs and regional OMS/WMS integrators distribute the tool; a historical returns diagnostic provides a low-meeting paid entry product.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Data connector and action queue that estimates fully loaded return cost, ranks SKU/root causes, recommends content or size interventions, flags abuse for human review and routes each returned unit to restock, outlet, repair or liquidation; SaaS plus savings fee.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The e-commerce operations or finance head pays by order volume plus an optional share of verified avoided loss; recurring paid events are refunds, standard-delivery reimbursement, handling, inspection, markdown and disposal.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A weekly return batch shows rising refunds, repeat reason codes, slow restocking or unsellable inventory, but the merchant cannot connect the loss to SKU content, sizing, supplier, carrier or customer behaviour.

founder_fit: Causal measurement, ranking and SKU-level prediction exploit data-science skills.
CEE localisation provides a regional wedge while the underlying workflow is scalable across the EU.
Agency and 3PL channels reduce direct merchant-by-merchant networking.
A fixed historical diagnostic can validate loss and willingness to pay before building live integrations.
risks: Abuse scores can unfairly penalise legitimate customers and must never auto-deny statutory rights.
Poor baselines can overstate savings and create contract disputes.
Platform or 3PL integration changes can raise maintenance cost.
Customer and order histories require GDPR minimisation and robust segregation.

structure.commercial_archetype: Loss-reduction analytics SaaS with optional savings share
structure.control_point: The SKU intervention backlog and per-unit disposition decision where refundable stock value is won or lost
structure.critical_dependency: Line-level return reasons and condition outcomes must be trustworthy, and merchants must implement recommended content or routing changes

thesis: Sell mid-sized Polish and CEE fashion, footwear and home-goods merchants an analytics layer that joins orders, product attributes, content changes, carrier events and return condition to identify avoidable returns and route returned stock to the highest-value disposition. Merchants already refund orders, reimburse standard delivery where required, pay reverse logistics and lose value on damaged or discarded stock; the offer targets those measured losses rather than generic dashboards.
title: Return-Loss Root Cause and Disposition Engine for CEE Merchants
uncertainties: The addressable number of CEE merchants with usable line-level condition data is unknown.
The proportion of returns preventable through product content, sizing or routing rather than customer preference must be measured.
It is unknown whether merchants will accept savings-share attribution or prefer fixed subscriptions.
Pricing, gross margin, customer targets and founder-wealth figures are assumptions.
